summary.text: Greenhouse gases are the gases in an atmosphere that absorb heat radiated by a planet's surface, raising its surface temperature.
Without them Earth's surface would average about −18 °C instead of today's 15 °C.
Since about 1750 human activity has raised carbon dioxide by over 50% and methane by 150%, and CO₂ now drives about three-quarters of global warming.

facts.label: Methane versus CO₂
facts.value: About 84 times stronger per mass over 20 years

items.prompt: Argon makes up 0.9% of the air yet traps no heat, while far scarcer carbon dioxide does. What makes the difference?

options.label: Argon atoms are too heavy to absorb heat
CO₂ mixes its elements, so its charge is uneven
CO₂ is a darker gas that soaks up sunlight
Argon sinks to the ground and never rises

items.explain: Argon is monatomic and transparent to thermal radiation, while CO₂'s atoms of different elements give an uneven charge that lets its vibrations interact with infrared.

items.prompt: Imagine every greenhouse gas vanished from Earth's air while sunlight stayed the same. About what would the average surface temperature be?

options.label: About 15 °C
About 30 °C
About −100 °C
About −18 °C

items.explain: Without greenhouse gases the surface would average about −18 °C rather than the present 15 °C.

items.prompt: Water vapor is the biggest greenhouse gas, yet large irrigation schemes barely change its global level. Why?

options.label: It leaves the air within about nine days
Oceans absorb all the extra vapor at once
It drifts up and escapes into space
Irrigation water never evaporates at all

items.explain: Irrigation can change local water vapor, but its short residence time of about nine days limits any global effect.

items.prompt: A factory releases one burst of methane and one burst of carbon dioxide. Which gas will linger in the atmosphere far longer?

options.label: Methane, by thousands of years
Both leave within a few years
Carbon dioxide, by a long way
Both stay about equally long

items.explain: Methane lasts about 12 years on average, while the carbon cycle takes thousands of years to fully absorb CO₂.

items.prompt: As greenhouse gases build up, the lower atmosphere warms. What happens to the thin upper atmosphere?

options.label: It warms even faster than the surface
It thickens as heat rises into it
It stays the same, as too little gas is there
It cools and shrinks

items.explain: Heat re-emitted in the thin upper layers tends to escape to space, so added greenhouse gases cool the upper atmosphere and make it shrink.

items.prompt: A change means more energy arrives at the top of the atmosphere than leaves it. How is this described, and what follows?

options.label: Positive forcing, leading to warming
Negative forcing, leading to warming
Positive forcing, leading to cooling
Negative forcing, leading to cooling

items.explain: Positive forcing, as from more greenhouse gases, means more energy arriving than leaving, which causes extra warming.
